evidence.source: dong_chinese
evidence.text: Originally was written the same as 作 (work). The 夂 (foot; movement) component was added later to distinguish the characters. The middle component 乍 was corrupted to look like 古, which caused later writers to reanalyze 做 as a compound of 亻and 故.

evidence.source: wiktionary
evidence.text:
Originally a vulgar variant of 作, written ⿰作攵. The component 乍 later corrupted into 古.
Colloquial form of the departing-tone variant of 作 (MC tsaH, “to do”), to differentiate from the checked-tone variant (now represented by 作). Loss of checked codas in Mandarin has resulted in homophony of the two.

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Ministry of Education, Taiwan)
evidence.text: The entry search result reports 《時俗杜撰字》:「作，俗作做。」 It also points to 《說文解字》 and cites a 《水滸傳》 example:「宋江教分作三起下山，只做去收捕梁山泊的官軍。」 This supports a traditional lexicographic account of 做 as a colloquial form of 作 and a literary attestation, but the page could not be opened to inspect its context or establish the edition/date of the quoted passage.
evidence.title: [A00206] 做 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 平凡社《普及版 字通》 via Kotobank
evidence.text: The entry identifies 作 as the standard graph, analyzes 作 as 乍 phonetic, calls 做 its vulgar/colloquial graph, and says 做 was often used in early modern usage. It reports that the Ming dictionary 《字彙》 included the graph. The page gives senses ‘to do/become’ and ‘make/work’; this is dictionary ordering, not proof of semantic chronology.
evidence.title: 做とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The entry states that, according to 《康熙字典》, 做 is in fact equivalent to 作. Its modern Mandarin field displays z- (the vowel/tone is image-rendered); its glosses include work, make, act, be, and do. This source does not provide a historical sequence of graphic stages or independently confirm 乍→古 corruption.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「做」

evidence.source: 中央研究院, 小學堂字形演變資料庫
evidence.text: The database describes 乍 as the older graph of 作, says the oracle-bone form represents the collar/front of an upper garment and making clothing, and says 人 was later added to form 作. It displays categories for oracle-bone, bronze, Chu bamboo/silk, and seal forms. This account concerns 乍 and 作, not the graphic history of 做; it does not establish the exact sound of an original depicted object.
evidence.title: 漢字「乍」：字形演變

evidence.source: 中央研究院, 小學堂字形演變資料庫
evidence.text: The comparison states that 作 forms in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions are written 乍 without 人, and that 乍 was historically interchangeable with 作. This supports a graphic and lexical relationship between 作 and 乍; it does not by itself show how 做 acquired its present 故-like right side.
evidence.title: 異體字「作」與「乍」的字義比較

evidence.source: Chinese Text Project, Kangxi dictionary quotation and cited references
evidence.text: The search result displays the Kangxi note: 《正字通》俗作字，字汇租去声。又音佐，不知作本有去入二音，分作做爲二，非。互见作字注。 It also provides later literary examples and bibliographic references to Kangxi, Cihai, and Hanyu Da Zidian. The opened page returned 403, so the search-result transcription is not treated as independently inspected primary text. The quotation itself disputes a simple claim that 作 and 做 necessarily began as separate characters distinguished by tone.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary quotation, search-result text only
evidence.title: 做 - Chinese Text Project

evidence.source: 中央研究院, local primary reading row cross-check
evidence.text: Local table has 作 twice: Middle Chinese ts ak / tsuH and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *[ts]ˤak / *[ts]ˤak-s, glossed ‘do, work.’ Exact 做, 乍, and 故 entries were not present in the inspected local table output. These values support only the recorded readings for 作; they do not establish an ancient phonetic role or the pronunciation of 做.
evidence.kind: local structured reading row; upstream click-through not verified
evidence.title: Baxter–Sagart reading table cross-check; official Unihan character page for click-through

evidence.source: 中央研究院, local primary reading row cross-check
evidence.text: Local table gives 乍 Middle Chinese dzraeH and Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese *[dz]ˤrak-s, glossed ‘suddenly.’ These are the table's readings for 乍 itself, not a reconstruction of the pictured garment or tool. Comparison with 作 (*[ts]ˤak / *[ts]ˤak-s) shows a potential historical sound relationship but distinct listed reconstructions; do not merge the entries or assume the readings prove the graph's phonetic role in 做.
evidence.kind: local structured reading row; upstream click-through not verified

evidence.text: The official Taiwan character record gives U+505A, the present decomposition ⿰亻故, and Mandarin zuò. This is current standardized graphic and pronunciation metadata, not evidence that the ancient graph was originally formed from 人 and 故 or that 故 is historically phonetic.

evidence.source: 全字庫 CNS11643, Taiwan Ministry of Digital Affairs
evidence.text: The character page explicitly encodes modern 做 as ⿰亻故 and gives Mandarin zuò. This confirms the modern graphic parse and reading only; it does not verify the dossier's claim that 乍 changed to 古 or that 故 was deliberately chosen as phonetic.
evidence.title: 字形資訊 - [做] 1-5878 - 全字庫 CNS11643

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry says 做 is not recorded in Shuowen and calls it a colloquial graph of 作, citing 字學三正: 「作，俗作做。」 It lists later senses with literary examples, including doing work, making, holding an office, and pretending. The examples’ order does not establish a semantic timeline.
evidence.kind: dictionary entry with cited historical sources
evidence.title: [A00206] 做 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Taiwan, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 作 entry; Shuowen analysis and variant notes
evidence.text: The entry reports the Shuowen analysis of 作 as 起也, 從人乍聲, and records a bronze form with 攴 as a variant of 作, citing 姞氏簋 and 虢文公鼎. This supports the historical 作/乍 relationship and the possibility of a 攴-bearing 作 variant; it does not establish that 做 descended from that graph or that 乍 changed into 古 in 做.
evidence.title: [A00123] 作 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Xiaoxuetang form evolution database
evidence.text: The database account describes 乍 as the older graph of 作 and interprets the oracle-bone form as an upper garment’s front/collar, connected with making clothing. This is the database’s interpretation of 乍; it does not identify the original spoken name of a depicted object or explain the later right side of 做.
evidence.title: 漢字「乍」：字形演變

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: No inspected primary inscription or manuscript attests 做's graphic stages; neither early oracle-bone nor bronze forms of 做 were established.

The dossier's specific claim that a form ⿰作攵 developed by corruption of 乍 into 古 is not independently supported by the inspected primary/authoritative pages. Modern IDS ⿰亻故 and lexicographic reports of 做 as a colloquial graph related to 作 are supported; the proposed intermediate and corruption remain unverified.

The historical account that 做 was a colloquial form of 作 has dictionary support, while a CText search-result quotation of Kangxi appears to dispute separating 作 and 做 by tone. CText could not be opened, so that competing quotation needs verification against an accessible edition.

A searchable MOE result cites a Water Margin example but the page was inaccessible, and the passage's edition/date was not determined. Kotobank reports inclusion in the Ming dictionary 《字彙》, but no precise publication date or earliest use in a dated document was inspected. Consequently earliest attested usage remains undetermined.

The shift from 作/乍 senses such as making, rising, or working to the broader modern senses of 做 (do, make, act, become) is not documented as a dated semantic sequence in the inspected sources. Dictionary gloss ordering is not chronology.

The Academia Sinica account interprets ancient 乍 pictorially as a garment collar/front, but its depicted referent and any object's original spoken name are not independently recoverable here. That limitation does not settle whether 乍 was later phonetic in 作.
Local Baxter–Sagart rows inspected for 作 and 乍 are preserved above; no matching rows for 做 or 故 were returned. Local rows are not externally clickable historical evidence.

The local Unihan_Readings.txt packet row for 做 is zuò. The prescribed official Unihan record endpoint was attempted but inaccessible. No local kMandarin rows for newly discussed 作, 乍, or 故 were recorded in the command output; the CNS page independently confirms current Mandarin zuò for 做, but no official Unihan pages for the other characters were successfully inspected.
No source's bulk reuse terms were reviewed because this research uses concise paraphrase and character-specific citations; no tracked extract is recommended.

No inspected primary inscription or manuscript establishes a graphic sequence for 做. The MOE dictionary says it is absent from Shuowen and traditionally a colloquial graph for 作, but the exact proposed ⿰作攵 → ⿰亻故 development is unverified.

The dossier’s specific claim that 乍 was corrupted into 古 in 做 is unsupported by the inspected pages. A 攴-bearing bronze variant of 作 is reported by the MOE 作 entry, but this does not demonstrate the claimed origin of 做.

The earliest secure attestation of 做 remains undetermined. MOE gives examples from works including 水滸傳 and cites 字學三正, but the accessible entry does not establish editions or dates for these cited instances. The CText/Kangxi page could not be opened to inspect the competing historical account.

Later senses are evidenced by literary quotations in the MOE entry, but no dated chain establishes when senses such as ‘make’, ‘do’, ‘become/serve as’, or ‘pretend’ developed. Dictionary ordering is not chronology.

The original referent and spoken name of the object interpreted as an upper garment front in 乍 are not independently recoverable here. That uncertainty does not establish or refute a later phonetic role in 作.

The official Unicode Unihan endpoint for 做 failed to open. Although local readings for 做, 作, and 乍 were supplied, official Unihan click-through records for the latter two were not inspected in this run.

Commons seal-script examples are modern vector redrawings. No suitable primary artifact image for 做 was established. The MOE page notes All Rights Reserved; it was used as evidence only. No tracked extract is recommended because reuse permission and added editorial value for a bulk extract were not both established.
